Being the insurer of the Pickup  vehicle bearing No.KA-51-D-5130  (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.7847/2023  Policy No.3313/00377880/000/00  Period of 06.04.2023 to 05.04.2024  (By Sri.K.Suresh, Advocate)

* *
 JUDGMENT The petitioners have filed this claim petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against respondents seeking compensation on account of death of the deceased Sri.Ashoka S/o Kalegowda, who died in Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under:
On 11.11.2023 at about 11.30 a.m, the deceased Ashoka was proceeding as a rider in a Bike bearing No.KA-13-EU-7362 near Hadenahalli Village, Shravanabelagola Hobli,
Channarayapattana Taluk, Hassan, at that time a Pickup vehicle bearing No.
KA-13-D-5130 driven by its driver, in rash and negligent manner, with high speed and dashed against deceased vehicle.
Due to this, the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries and died at the spot itself.
The petitioners have spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards transportation, funeral and final rituals.

Prior to accident the deceased was hale (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.7847/2023 and healthy and was aged about 38 years and was working as waterman and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m and he was contributing entire income to welfare of the family.

Due to this accident,
the petitioners have lost the bread winner of family.

The petitioner No.1 being wife,
petitioner No.2 being son and petitioners No.3 and 4 being the parents of the deceased have lost caring and loving husband, father as well as son, since they were depending on the deceased income.

The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of above said offending Pickup vehicle by its driver and in this regard the Shravanabelagola Traffic Police have registered a case against driver of said offending vehicle.
The respondent No.1 being the owner and respondent No.2 Geetha vs Uttam Glass House on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111021899/
2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.51,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a and costs.
03. On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their counsels and filed written statement.

04. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioners and further denied the alleged accident, negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, age, income,
occupation (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.7847/2023 of the deceased and nature of the injuries sustained by the deceased and treatment taken by the deceased and contended that the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of rider of Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-13-EU-7362 who rode the vehicle in high speed, in zig-zag manner and had crossed the divider line from the other side of the road and dashed the Pickup vehicle and this respondent admits that it is the RC owner of offending Pickup vehicle and same is insured with respondent No.2 Insurance Company vide Policy No.3313/00377880/000/00 which is valid from 06.04.2023 to 05.04.2024 and the driver had a valid driving licence.

The compensation claimed is exaggerated and pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.1.
05.

The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioners and denied alleged accident, death of deceased, age, avocation and income of deceased, dependency of the petitioners and expenses incurred by the petitioners and contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident and the respondent No.l has handed over the possession of the vehicle to the said driver and therefore, has contravened the provisions of (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.7847/2023 M.V. Act and committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy and admits that this respondent has issued a policy of insurance in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of Mahindra Goods vehicle bearing No.KA-13-D-5130 and the liability is limited to terms and conditions of the policy and denies very occurred of the accident and involvement of Mahindra Goods vehicle and said vehicle did not involve in the accident nor caused accidental injuries to the deceased and contended that the rider of the Motor Cycle was not holding a valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident and the petitioners in collison with the jurisdiction Police have created false records and story in order to get compensation and lodged a false complaint.
The petition is bad for non-joinder of proper and necessary parties.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive, exaggerated.
Hence, pray for dismiss the petition against respondent No.2 with costs.
06. On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, this tribunal has framed the following Issues:-
ISSUES 01. Whether petitioners prove that they are the LRs/dependents of deceased Sri.Ashoka S/o Kalegowda?

3 02. Whether petitioners prove that deceased Sri.Ashoka S/o Kalegowda was died in RTA arising out of the accident alleged to have been taken place on 11.11.2023 at about 11.30 a.m, near Hadenahalli Village, Shravanabelagona Hobli,
Channarayapatana Taluk, Hassan, due to rash and negligence driving of Pickup vehicle by the driver bearing registration No.KA-13-D-5130 as alleged in the petition?
03.
Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
04. What order or award?
07. The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 is examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 18 documents as Ex.P.1 to 18 and closed her side evidence.

Despite sufficient opportunity,
the respondents have not lead evidence, hence, respondents evidence is taken as nil and closed their side evidence.
08.
The counsels for the petitioners and respondent No.2 argued on the main matter.
Despite sufficient opportunity, the respondent No.1 has not advanced its arguments, hence respondent No.1 arguments is taken as heard and perused the records.

My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS 10. Issues No.1 and 2:- Since these two issues are interconnected to each other and in order to avoid repetition of facts and appreciation of evidence on record, these two issues are taken together for common consideration and discussion.
11. The petitioners in order to prove their case, the petitioner No.1 is examined as PW.1 and in her chief-examination evidence she has reiterated the petition averments.

Though she has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.2 counsel, but nothing has been brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioners regarding rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, death of deceased and the petitioners are not the dependents and legal representatives of the deceased and during the cross-examination
she denied to the suggestion that (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.7847/2023 the accident was occurred due to negligence of her husband who rode his Motor Cycle without switching indicator or signal.

sentences.text: Apart from the oral evidence, the petitioners have got marked 18 documents as Ex.P.1 to 18 on their behalf.
Ex.P.1 is copy of FIR filed by the Shravanabelagola Traffic Police against driver of Pickup vehicle for his rash and negligent driving, caused accident and death of deceased.
Ex.P.2 is copy of Complaint.
Ex.P.3 is copy of Spot Mahazar.
Ex.P.4 is copy of Sketch.
Ex.P.5 is copy of Inquest panchanama of deceased Ashoka.
Ex.P.6 is copy of Post mortem report of deceased Ashoka wherein it is stated that cause of death is due to haemorrhagic shock as a result of head injury sustained.
Ex.P.7 is copy of statement of complainant Paramesha.
Ex.P.8 is copy of statement of eye-witness Jagadisha.
Ex.P.9 is copy of Notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act issued to the owner of the offending vehicle.

Ex.P.10 is copy of Reply to notice wherein the owner of the offending pickup vehicle has stated that he is the owner of the said vehicle and one Faheed Ahmed was driving the said vehicle and he had a valid driving licence as on the date of accident.
Ex.P.11 and 12 are copies of IMV reports which discloses that both vehicles are involved in the (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.7847/2023 accident and both vehicles are damaged.

Ex.P.13 is copy of Charge sheet which discloses that the Investigation Officer after thorough investigation has submitted Charge sheet against driver of the Mahindra Pickup Goods vehicle for his rash and negligent driving and causing accident and causing death of deceased.
Ex.P.14 is the copy of Aadhaar card of petitioner No.1.
Ex.P.15 is the copy of Aadhaar card of petitioner No.2.
Ex.P.16 is the copy of Aadhaar card of petitioner No.3.
Ex.P.17 is the copy of Aadhaar card of petitioner No.4 and Ex.P.18 is the copy of Aadhaar card of deceased Ashoka.

13. On going through the entire oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioners, it is clearly establishes that petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 is the son, petitioner No.3 is the mother and petitioner No.4 is the father of the deceased and they are legal representatives and dependents on the income of the deceased.

It is further established and proved that the deceased Ashoka was died in road traffic accident that occurred on 11.11.2023 at about 11.30 a.m, near Hadenahalli Village, Shravanabelagola Hobli, Channarayapattana Taluk, Hassan, due to rash and negligent driving of Pickup vehicle bearing No.KA- (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.7847/2023 13-D-5130 by its driver.
Accordingly, Issues No.1 and 2 are answered in the affirmative.
14. Issue No.3:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the death of the deceased Ashoka, who died in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

The PW.1/petitioner No.1 has stated that prior to accident deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 38 years and was working as waterman and earning Rs.50,000/- p.m and have spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards transportation, funeral and final rituals.
Due to death of deceased, they have lost earning member of their family and lost love and affection.
15. It is the duty of the petitioners to prove age, avocation and income of the deceased as on the date of accident.
The petitioners have not produced any birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card of the deceased to show the exact date of birth of the deceased.
However, they have produced Ex.P.18 Aadhaar card of deceased.

Eventhough the said document is not authenticated document for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of other evidence, said document can be relied Geetha vs Uttam Glass House on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111021899/
5 upon and according to which his date of birth is mentioned as (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.7847/2023 01.01.1985.
The alleged accident occurred on 11.11.2023.
Hence, it appears that as on the date of accident the deceased is aged 38 years.
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the age of the deceased as 38 years as on the date of accident.

As per the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors. case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 36 to 40 years is 15.
16.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So far as avocation and income of deceased is concerned, the petitioners have not produced any documents.

Therefore, in the absence of satisfactory evidence regarding avocation and income of the deceased, this tribunal has relied upon notional income as per the chart issued by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru and as per norms for the year 2023 the notional income is Rs.16,000/- p.m and hence, this tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.16,000/-
p.m and it is multiplied by 12.
17.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case, the future prospects or (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.7847/2023 additional income should be added to monthly income of the deceased.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Since deceased was aged about 38 years at the time of accident and was self employee,
40% income should be added to the monthly income towards future prospects which would be result in the income to be (16,000 + 6,400) = Rs.22,400/-.
18.

In the case on hand, undoubtedly the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 is the son,
petitioner No.3 is the mother and petitioner No.4 is the father and they are dependents on the income of the deceased and there is four dependents, it is appropriate to deduct 1/4th of the income of the deceased towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and then his monthly income would be (22,400 - 5,600) = Rs.16,800/-.
The income of the deceased for the purpose of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.16,800/-.
As the deceased was aged about 38 years, the multiplier of 15 would have to be applied.
Consequently the claimants would be entitled for a sum of Rs.30,24,000/- (Rs.16,800 x 12 x 15) towards loss of dependency.

19. In view of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & Others case, in respect to loss of estate, loss of (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.7847/2023 consortium and funeral expenses, the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every 3 years.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, in the head of loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses, 10% is enhanced for period of every 3 years.
20. The claimant No.1 is the wife, claimant No.2 is the son, claimant No.3 is the mother and claimant No.4 is the father of the deceased.

Therefore, petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs.52,000/-
towards loss of spousal consortium.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram alias Churu Ram reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130, the petitioner No.2 is entitled for Rs.40,000/- towards loss of parental consortium and the petitioners No.3 and 4 are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of filial consortium and petitioners are entitled for Rs.19,500/- each towards loss of estate and funeral expenses and transportation of dead body.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram alias Churu Ram reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Considering the facts and circumstances of the Geetha vs Uttam Glass House on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111021899/
6 case and noticing the number of dependents and 1/4th of the income taken into consideration towards the personal and living expenses of the deceased, this Tribunal has placed reliance on ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.7847/2023 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & others case has calculated compensation as under;
 Sl. Head of Amount in  No. Compensation Rs.
 1. Loss of Dependency 30,24,000-00  (After deducting 1/4th of  the income towards  personal and living  expenses)
 2. Loss of spousal 52,000-00  consortium (petitioner  No.1)
 3. Loss of parental 40,000-00  consortium (petitioner  No.2)
 4. Loss of filial consortium 80,000-00  (petitioners No.3 and 4)
 5. Loss of estate 19,500-00

Accordingly I hold that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.32,35,000/-
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

Regarding liability:- Though the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal and filed written statements and taken several defences, but despite sufficient opportunity they have not lead any evidence to disprove the case of the petitioners and to prove their contentions.

Further, the respondent No.1 in its written statement at para 9 admits that it is the owner of the offending vehicle and same was insured with respondent No.2 and policy of the offending vehicle is valid as on the date of accident
The respondent No.2 Insurance Company in its written statement at para 6 admits issuance of insurance policy in respect of offending vehicle and the same is valid as on the date of accident.
But the respondent No.2 has not lead any evidence or placed any material to show that the owner or driver of the offending vehicle have violated terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

However, since policy of offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending Geetha vs Uttam Glass House on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111021899/
7 vehicle shall pay above said compensation amount of Rs.32,35,000/- with interest at the rate of (SCCH-3) 17 M.V.C.No.7847/2023 6% p.a to the petitioners from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, this Issue is answered partly in the affirmative.
23. Issue No.4:

In view of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.32,35,000/- (Rupees Thirty two lakhs and thirty five thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

The petitioner No.1 being the wife, petitioner No.2 being the son, petitioner No.3 being the mother and petitioner No.4 being the father of the deceased were apportioned the compensation in the ratio of 40-20-20-20, in the award amount together with interest.

The petitioners No.1 to 4 are entitled to get release 70% each of the award amount through E-payment directly to their account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% each shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

Therefore, in the absence of satisfactory evidence regarding avocation and income of the deceased, this tribunal has relied upon notional income as per the chart issued by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru and as per norms for the year 2023 the notional income is Rs.16,000/- p.m and hence, this tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.16,000/-
p.m and it is multiplied by 12.
17.
In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case, the future prospects or (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.7847/2023 additional income should be added to monthly income of the deceased.
19. In view of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & Others case, in respect to loss of estate, loss of (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.7847/2023 consortium and funeral expenses, the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every 3 years.
Accordingly, in the head of loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses, 10% is enhanced for period of every 3 years.
In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram alias Churu Ram reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130, the petitioner No.2 is entitled for Rs.40,000/- towards loss of parental consortium and the petitioners No.3 and 4 are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of filial consortium and petitioners are entitled for Rs.19,500/- each towards loss of estate and funeral expenses and transportation of dead body.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
